newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate edges up to 10.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate edges up to 10.5 pct.

text.p: The average price of money on Croatia's money market edged up 20 basis points to 10.5 percent on Monday, boosted by higher interest on term loans for fresh borrowings despite weaker demand.
Total settlements shrank to under 41 million kuna from 70.9 million and only 15.5 million were new loans, dealers said.
They put interbank rates at 9.0-15 percent, with call money rising to 9.75 from 9.0 percent. Insurers charged a steady 8.0 percent for their placements.
Commercial banks borrowed a meagre 6.2 million kuna in overnight trade at the week-end.

The central bank said it still had no foreign exchange operations. Its kuna midrates for Tuesday eased slightly to 5.4359 and 3.5685 against the dollar and the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
